title: Symbolic Regression via MDLformer-Guided Search: From Minimizing Prediction Error to Minimizing Description Length

contributions.purpose: Solve the low recovery rate of heuristic-search symbolic regression, caused by prediction error not decreasing monotonically as the search approaches the target formula (SR lacks an optimal substructure under prediction-error objective).
contributions.mechanism: Propose a new search objective based on the minimum description length (MDL) instead of prediction error; MDL decreases monotonically toward the target formula, giving the search an optimal substructure.
contributions.evaluation: Conceptual/qualitative motivation (Figure 1): MSE of candidate formulas does not decrease monotonically along the route to target f*, whereas MDL does; validated downstream by the recovery-rate experiments.
contributions.source_quote: To solve this problem, we propose a novel search objective based on the minimum description length, which reflects the distance from the target and decreases monotonically as the search approaches the correct form of the target formula.

contributions.purpose: MDL is proven incomputable, so an accurate MDL estimate of arbitrary input data is needed to make the MDL objective usable.
contributions.mechanism: Design MDLformer, a Transformer-based neural network (embedder + encoder + attention pooling + MLP readout) trained cross-modally with a primary MDL-prediction loss and an auxiliary numeric/symbolic latent-space alignment loss, over ~131 million symbolic-numeric pairs using a two-step training strategy.
contributions.evaluation: Trained on over 130 million symbolic-numeric pairs; further analysis demonstrates scalable and robust MDL prediction (Section 5 analysis).
contributions.domain: Symbolic regression / neural network property estimation
contributions.source_quote: To estimate the minimum description length of any input data, we design a neural network, MDLformer, which enables robust and scalable estimation through large-scale training.

contributions.purpose: Turn the MDL objective and MDLformer into a working symbolic regression method that recovers correct mathematical forms.
contributions.mechanism: Implement SR4MDL, a Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) symbolic regression method that maintains candidate subformulas and uses MDLformer's output in the UCB search objective; final transformation fitted with a simple linear function.
contributions.evaluation: Recovers ~50 of 133 formulas across two benchmark datasets, outperforming state-of-the-art by 43.92%; robust to noise (10% noise recovery still exceeds other methods' noise-free recovery); generalizes on 122 unseen black-box problems with lower description length and higher accuracy.
contributions.source_quote: With the MDLformer's output as the search objective, we implement a symbolic regression method, SR4MDL, that can effectively recover the correct mathematical form of the formula.

self_declared_provenance.quote: We generate symbolic formulas with the algorithm proposed by Kamienny et al. (2022) to ensure diversity
The auxiliary objective, proposed by Meidani et al. (2023), aims to facilitate a mutual understanding of both numeric and symbolic domains and thus empower better cross-modal prediction.

In this work, we implement our method based on the Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) (Browne et al., 2012) ... The vast majority of our implementations are consistent with the existing practice of using MCTS for symbolic regression (Sun et al., 2022), except that the upper confidence bound (UCB) to guide the search is based on MDLformer's output

As a comparison, our method can also be regarded as a method of recursively simplifying the target function ... Identifying subformulas based on MDLformer's output rather than hand-designed rules, our method does not rely on specific prior knowledge and is more robust to noise. (contrast to AIFeynman, Udrescu & Tegmark, 2020)

notes: Positive-result heavy paper (accept). Reported robustness result is notable: recovery rate under 10% noise still exceeds competitors' noise-free recovery. Absolute recovery is modest (~50/133 ≈ 38%), and the 43.92% figure is a relative improvement over SOTA, not an absolute rate. No explicit negative/tie/trade-off results found in abstract/intro/related work.
